verdict.rationale: Cactus documents its own workflow for building task-specialized models: you generate tool-calling training data from your tools and a product description, fine-tune Needle 3 (locally via LoRA or on hosted GPUs), and then run it with your own decorated tool functions. This is model specialization for specific tasks rather than a configurable 'assistant' object, and hands-on reports show weak accuracy for fine-tuned Needle 3 (32.2% correct tool shape) and note it must match the use case exactly. Missing for 10: a first-class custom assistant configuration feature (persona, instructions, saved assistant profiles), evidence that fine-tuned specialists perform reliably, and documentation of managing multiple assistants.

support.subject: As a power-user, I can create specialized custom assistants configured for specific tasks

citations.quote: Generate tool-calling training data, fine-tune Needle 3, and download the resulting models.
POST /generations with your tools, a count of 100 to 10,000 examples, and ideally a product description and a few example messages.
Decorate a function: the signature gives the argument types, the docstring is the tool description, and run() completes the loop
Free: $0 for local LoRA fine-tuning with the open-source package.
